reviews.support: מַשָּׂא דְבַר־יְהוָה governs the speech; 1:2 begins אָהַבְתִּי ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם בַּמָּה, 1:5 closes with seeing and saying, and 1:6 shifts to a son-servant analogy plus explicit priestly vocative. The first objection supplies the heading's complete claim-counterclaim-demonstration-result movement. Edom's rebuild counterclaim and reversal culminate in 1:5 recognition, while לָכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים at 1:6 changes addressee and accusation.
counterevidence: Mal.1.1 is a superscription distinct from direct speech in 1:2.

reviews.support: The priestly vocative and בַּמֶּה objection at 1:6 open the charge; renewed objections, defective offerings, governor comparison, rejection, nations contrast, and וְאָרוּר נוֹכֵל ... כִּי מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל אָנִי carry it to curse and rationale. Verses 1:6-9 establish despised name and polluted altar. Verse 1:10 pivots to temple-door wish and worldwide-name contrast; 1:12-13 turns that contrast against the priests, and 1:14 supplies the deceiver curse and great-name reason. The samekh after 1:13 is genuine counterevidence, so the larger unit is retained but treatment is held.
counterevidence: OSHB and UXLC place samekh after Mal.1.13.
Mal.1.10 is a marked wish-rejection-nations turn.
Mal.1.14 follows the marker but echoes 1:11's great-name rationale.

challenges.claim: Should the primary surface remain Mal.1.6-1.14 as the complete disputation, or should the samekh authorize dependent Mal.1.6-1.13 and Mal.1.14 surfaces with mandatory Mal.1.6-1.14 hydration? The former preserves accusation-to-curse logic; the latter preserves textual presentation without making 1:14 an independent proof text.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Mal.1.6-Mal.1.9 | Mal.1.10-Mal.1.14: The second panel resumes the polluted-table accusation; both children require the whole dispute.; Mal.1.6-Mal.1.13 | Mal.1.14: The samekh supports presentation separation, but standalone 1:14 loses the sacrificial deceit and functions as the dispute's curse coda.
counterevidence: OSHB and UXLC place samekh after Mal.1.13.
Mal.1.10 is a marked wish-rejection-nations turn.
Mal.1.14 follows the marker but echoes 1:11's great-name rationale.

reviews.support: וְעַתָּה אֲלֵיכֶם הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת הַכֹּהֲנִים restarts at 2:1; 2:4 names covenant purpose, 2:5-7 gives Levi's ideal, וְאַתֶּם at 2:8 contrasts failure, and a pe after 2:9 closes consequence. Threatened curse establishes why the command was sent concerning Levi. The ideal mouth/path/messenger panel is the comparison for adversative priestly failure and public consequence. The explicit command onset and pe define a child distinct from the offering dispute while the larger priestly parent remains mandatory.
counterevidence: The priestly addressee continues from 1:6.
Mal.2.5 and 2:8 mark useful dependent panels.

The ideal mouth/path/messenger panel is the comparison for adversative priestly failure and public consequence. The explicit command onset and pe define a child distinct from the offering dispute while the larger priestly parent remains mandatory.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Retain Mal.2.1-Mal.2.9 as the surface, or require it automatically whenever Mal.2.1-Mal.2.4 is retrieved.
counterevidence: The priestly addressee continues from 1:6.
Mal.2.5 and 2:8 mark useful dependent panels.

reviews.support: First-person-plural הֲלוֹא ... לְכֻלָּנוּ and מַדּוּעַ נִבְגַּד change voice and scope at 2:10; judgment ends at a pe after 2:12 before וְזֹאת שֵׁנִית in 2:13. Shared-father and creator questions frame Judah's profanation as one communal accusation, and 2:12 supplies consequence. The pe plus explicit second-act formula makes 2:10-12 a real child while hydration preserves the whole treachery complex.
counterevidence: Repeated בגד links 2:10-12 and 2:13-16.
Father/creator referents and עֵר וְעֹנֶה are translation hot zones.

reviews.support: וְזֹאת שֵׁנִית תַּעֲשׂוּ opens a second act after pe; וַאֲמַרְתֶּם עַל־מָה gives the objection, repeated בגד and נשמרתם bind answer and warning, and samekh after 2:16 closes. Altar tears pose the consequence, 'why?' introduces Yahweh's covenant witness, and compressed 2:15-16 repeats guard-your-spirit and treachery language. Syntax is difficult, but the explicit onset and closing marker define the outer unit without deciding translation or law.
counterevidence: Mal.2.15-16 has severe clause, subject, and translation ambiguity.
Covenant and treachery language links backward.

reviews.support: 2:17 opens הוֹגַעְתֶּם ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם and asks אַיֵּה אֱלֹהֵי הַמִּשְׁפָּט; 3:1 answers הִנְנִי שֹׁלֵחַ מַלְאָכִי, 3:2 tests endurance, and 3:5 returns to לַמִּשְׁפָּט as swift witness. The WEB chapter edge falls between complaint and answer. Way-preparation, coming, endurance, refining, restored offerings, and judgment resolve the claims that evil is pleasing and justice absent; 3:6 then begins a new first-person grounding and return dispute.
counterevidence: Mal.3.1 has strong הִנְנִי onset as an answer child.
Messenger, Lord, covenant-messenger, and first-person references complicate translation.

reviews.support: כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה לֹא שָׁנִיתִי grounds 3:6; שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי and בַּמֶּה נָשׁוּב lead to the 3:8 robbery objection, הָבִיאוּ and וּבְחָנוּנִי supply remedy, and nations coda ends at samekh after 3:12. The broad return summons asks how to return, and the tithe accusation answers with wrong, command, test, crop protection, and nations recognition. Splitting at 3:8 leaves the objection unanswered; splitting after the imperative loses promised result.
counterevidence: Mal.3.8 begins a fresh question and objection as a dependent child.
Mal.3.6 may bridge backward as well as ground the return dispute.

reviews.support: חָזְקוּ עָלַי דִּבְרֵיכֶם and וַאֲמַרְתֶּם open at 3:13; אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי יְהוָה turns to an answering group in 3:16, and 3:18 closes with servant/non-servant discernment before samekh. The claim that service is futile is answered narratively: fearers speak, Yahweh hears, a record is written, and possession and sparing lead to discernment between the same service categories. The 3:16 response is a child, but it is the accusation's lexical and rhetorical answer.
counterevidence: אָז at 3:16 changes actors.
Samekh after 3:18 marks presentation break.
כִּי הִנֵּה at 4:1 makes the next child causally dependent.

reviews.support: WEB 4:1 is MT/WLC 3:19 and begins כִּי הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא after samekh; three verses contrast wrongdoers and name-fearers and close at pe after MT/WLC 3:21 before זִכְרוּ. Causal כִּי links the day oracle to 3:18 discernment, so it is not an independent fragment. Yet samekh before, complete burning/healing contrast, and pe after WEB 4:3 justify a dependent surface with mandatory 3:13-4:3 hydration.
counterevidence: Initial כִּי makes 4:1 dependent on 3:18.
WEB chapter division has no independent Hebrew authority; this is MT/WLC 3:19-21.

reviews.support: After pe at MT/WLC 3:21, זִכְרוּ תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה commands remembrance; הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ begins the paired sending, and 4:6 supplies reconciliation purpose and פֶּן ... חֵרֶם risk. The coda pairs what Israel must remember with what the speaker will send before the day. Reciprocal heart-turning and the lest-clause are purpose and risk, so neither panel surfaces alone. The preceding pe and new commands distinguish the coda without granting WEB chapter authority.
counterevidence: זִכְרוּ and הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ introduce distinguishable child panels.
Named figures prompt later reuse, but reuse is not local splitting authority.
